It doesn’t sound like a serious ailment, but it qualifies as a big deal because it involves the health of the San Francisco 49ers’ franchise quarterback: Brock Purdy didn’t practice Wednesday because of an ankle injury.

Head coach Kyle Shanahan termed Purdy “day-to-day” after he was injured during the second quarter of the 49ers’ 35-10 win over the Vikings last Sunday in Mexico City. Shanahan said Purdy didn’t have a high ankle sprain, which typically sidelines players for multiple weeks, and that Purdy’s injury didn’t impact Shanahan’s play-calling after he was checked on the sideline. Purdy was observed in the locker room Wednesday walking without a noticeable limp.

“They always tell you when someone has (an injury), but then they come back and they’re like, ‘Hey, checked out. He should be fine,’” Shanahan said. “He didn’t miss any plays.”

Purdy appeared to be injured with 11 seconds left in the second quarter when defensive tackle Jalen Redmond rolled up on his left ankle while pressuring Purdy on a play in which Purdy was flagged for intentional grounding.
